front: Name the four types of pathogen.
Give a named bacterial disease and a named viral disease.
back: Bacterial: Salmonella or gonorrhoea. Viral: measles or HIV.

front: What is a vector, in the context of disease?
back: Something that carries a pathogen without being infected itself — e.g. mosquitoes carrying malaria.

front: Name the three ways white blood cells respond to a pathogen.
How does a vaccine protect someone?
back: Triggers antibody production (and memory cells) without causing the disease, so the body responds much faster if it meets the real pathogen later.

front: Why don't antibiotics work on viruses?
back: Viruses reproduce inside human cells in a completely different way to bacteria, so antibiotics (which target bacteria) have no effect.

front: What natural source did digitalis (a heart drug) come from?
What natural source did aspirin come from?
Who discovered penicillin, and from what?
back: Alexander Fleming, from the mould Penicillium.

front: What is a major consequence of antibiotic overuse?
back: The development of antibiotic-resistant strains of bacteria.
